rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration with key components (ViT-L image encoder, PCA RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) to establish performance and isolate the impact of these choices. This clarifies the effectiveness of advanced encoders and fusion strategies, which are critical for multimodal performance.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves 0.5856 validation accuracy. This experiment tests changing fusion from weighted to concat while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the effect of fusion method. It directly addresses whether the fusion strategy significantly impacts performance, providing critical insight into model design without altering multiple parameters.

Existing evidence shows that config_007 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves higher accuracy than config_001. This experiment tests whether changing the image encoder to resnet50 and aggregation to avgpool (config_003) improves performance, isolating the impact of these design choices. It balances exploration by comparing key components while maintaining similarity to the current best configuration.

Existing evidence shows that using ResNet50 image encoder, Avgpool aggregation, and Concat fusion (config_003) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from PCA_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a different representation method) while keeping other parameters fixed isolates the impact of the RNA encoder choice. This clarifies whether the RNA encoder significantly affects performance, a critical design decision, without changing multiple variables simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows config_002 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieves the highest accuracy (0.6315). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (while keeping other components identical) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, and builds on the strong baseline of config_002.

Existing evidence shows that config_016 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with ViT and switching aggregation to transformer, which could reveal if these changes improve performance. It isolates the impact of advanced encoders and aggregation methods while retaining the successful RNA encoder and fusion strategy.

Existing evidence shows config_020 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (while keeping RNA/image encoders and aggregation method identical) impacts performance. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy, which is critical for multimodal models, and builds on the promising direction of config_020.

Existing evidence shows that config_020 (scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether switching to resnet50 image encoder and concat fusion (while keeping scvi_n200 RNA and transformer aggregation) affects performance. It isolates the impact of image encoder and fusion method, which are critical design choices with limited prior evidence. This balances exploitation (building on scvi_n200's success) and exploration (testing alternative image encoders/fusion strategies).

The existing evidence shows that using 'transformer' aggregation and 'weighted' fusion with 'scvi_n200' RNA and 'imagenet_vit_l' image encoder achieves the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether changing the image encoder to 'resnet50' (a simpler, less complex model) while keeping other parameters the same affects performance. It isolates the impact of the image encoder choice, which is critical for understanding whether more complex models are necessary, and balances exploitation of current high-performing components with exploration of alternatives.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (config_020: 0.725). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt while keeping other components the same, isolating the effect of the RNA representation. It balances exploration of new encoders with exploitation of the current top-performing setup, addressing uncertainty about whether newer encoders (scgpt) could improve performance without changing multiple parameters.
